flags.headline: Argentina country risk breaks above 600bps for first time since April; Merval falls 5th straight session
flags.detail: No new U.S. equity session (Saturday) so SUPV itself did not trade further, but the underlying macro deterioration behind this AMBER flag intensified over the weekend reporting window: JPMorgan's Argentina country-risk gauge rose a 10th consecutive session to 609bps (session high 628bps) on Friday 9/25, its highest level since April and its first close above 600 in about six months. The Merval fell a 5th consecutive session, -1.57% to 2,893,751, concentrated in banks and financial services -- Supervielle's own sector. The peso weakened to ~1,524/USD. No Supervielle-specific news. This is the same 'post-election reform trade cooling' dynamic flagged the last two sessions, now accelerating rather than resolving; worth the desk's attention heading into Monday's open even though no new SUPV print exists yet.
flags.thesis_link: Matches key_risk: 'Argentine macroeconomic instability -- inflation volatility, peso devaluation risk, and potential policy reversals around midterm elections could reverse reform progress and compress bank margins.'
